routes: /settings/api-access (real APIAccessPanel consumer in an isolated HTTP fixture)
states: Playwright 1.56.1, Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and WebKit 26.0; desktop light and narrow dark. Comparable parent/final captures use the same synthetic token, operation, viewport, theme and draft. Scope states: initial, failed response, underlying inventory and final recovered inventory.

PATCH applies monitoring:read but returns 502. Parent retains Full access inventory and Save scopes; final closes the stale dialog, focuses an explicit uncertainty notice, shows Unknown rather than zero/unchanged, and blocks further writes until an accepted read.

Chromium additionally exercises applied create, rename and revoke with lost responses at both viewports. Parent bytes for those comparisons are loaded from exact git-show snapshots of these two files at base_sha, with unchanged current consumers; scope baseline used the original assigned source before editing.

Safe API HTTP stubs plus inert resource/WebSocket inputs, real APIAccessPanel/state/dialogs/SecurityAPI/API client/CSS/toasts. This is not installed account, production-bundle or reporter recovery proof.
interactions: All four scope cases send exactly one PATCH with monitoring:read and preserve the existing organization and CSRF headers. No automatic mutation or read replay. The read-only Check token inventory action survives a failed GET; double activation coalesces and the write gate persists through a delayed GET. Accepted inventory shows the applied scope with draft name/preset intact.

Additional create/rename/revoke cases each send exactly one write, then only one deliberate GET. Keyboard Enter activates recovery. Lost create values are never revealed; the notice tells users to revoke an issued token whose value was not received. Successful read restores truthful names/absence and enables deliberate actions.
No page errors or horizontal overflow in completed cases. All retained capture files are inspected natively; browser checks and initial fixture/selector failures are retained separately.
